rules.statement: When a change alters infrastructure, settings or steps that an operational runbook describes, update the runbook in the same change.
rules.why: The runbook is a living document that must stay accurate for anyone reproducing the platform from scratch, so it has to change together with what it describes.
rules.check: A diff that changes bootstrap infrastructure code, required manual settings or token permissions without a matching edit to the runbook that documents them.

rules.statement: Pin every third-party GitHub Action and reusable workflow reference to a full-length commit SHA, not a tag or branch.
rules.why: Someone can move a tag to point at different code; a full SHA cannot be swapped.
rules.check: `uses:` lines in workflow files that reference `@v1`, `@main` or any ref other than a 40-character commit SHA.

rules.statement: Never commit API tokens, passphrases or other credentials to repository files; supply them only through environment variables or a secret store.
rules.why: The infrastructure repository is public, and bootstrap credentials are supposed to exist only for the duration of a shell session.
rules.check: Tokens, keys, passphrases or secret-looking literals in committed files such as tfvars, config or scripts, or code that writes a secret to a file inside the repository.

rules.statement: Do not create long-lived cloud IAM users or access keys for automation; CI must authenticate through federated OIDC roles that issue short-lived credentials.
rules.why: CI uses GitHub OIDC, so standing access keys aren't needed and would only add credentials that can leak.
rules.check: IaC that declares IAM users, access keys or static cloud credentials for pipelines (e.g. `aws_iam_user`, `aws_iam_access_key`) where an OIDC-assumed role would do.

rules.statement: Grant cloud access permissions to groups, never directly to individual users.
rules.why: With group grants, adding or removing an administrator takes one membership change.
rules.check: Permission-set or role assignments in IaC whose principal is a single user and not a group.
